title: Spanish Rice Stuffed Bell Peppers
ingredients: 4 large bell peppers (any color or a combination of colors) - cored, seeded, tops reserved
1 cup fresh corn kernels or thawed frozen corn
1 (5.6 ounce) package Knorr® Fiesta Sides™ - Spanish Rice
1 cup shredded Mexican cheese blend or Monterey Jack cheese, divided
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees (190 degrees C). Spray an 8- or 9-inch square baking dish with cooking spray, and set aside. Finely chop pepper tops, and set aside.

Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Cook chorizo and corn until corn begins to turn golden and chorizo begins to brown about 5 minutes. Add ground beef and cook until browned, about 10 minutes.

Stir 2 cups water, Knorr® Fiesta Sides™ - Spanish Rice, and chopped pepper tops to the skillet. Cook according to package directions. Stir in 3/4 cup cheese and let stand 2 minutes. Stuff peppers equally with rice mixture and arrange in the prepared baking dish. Add 2 tablespoons water to the baking dish and cover tightly with foil.
Bake until peppers are tender, about 45 minutes. Remove and discard the foil. Sprinkle peppers evenly with remaining 1/4 cup cheese. Continue to bake until the cheese melts, about 2 minutes.

most_helpful_positive_review.text: It was really good something kinda new for us to eat but it was great. Definitely adding this on the menu.

featured_tweaks.text: We LOVE this dish. We use turkey sausage instead of chorizo and we add in chopped onion as well. It’s now a HUGE staple in my house. Can’t get enough of it! And we use the leftover stuffing stuff for burritos the next day! Love it!!

Great recipe, only changes I made were that I used mild Italian sausage instead of chorizo because I could get any at the time. I also added half a chopped sweet onion and 2 cloves of fresh minced garlic, some sea salt and pepper. But great recipe and very flavour full and I will definitely be making this again!

My husband said these are the best stuffed peppers he's ever had. I could not find Knorr "Fiesta Sides," I went with Knorr Spanish Rice (the other choices were mexican Rice or Taco Rice. I added diced onion at the very beginning of cooking. Also, I used chopped beef instead of hamburger. I think this is something we will have a lot and I may even take it to potlucks.
I did add diced green onions , excellent flavor!

I added garlic to the onions and sautéed them together. Wasn’t able to get a pic, had them on the counter covered up, left the house and when I got home everybody had already eaten them! So they musta been good!

Fun and delicious! I used a pound of beef and a 9oz package of chorizo so I had a bunch of filling. I made 5 peppers (2 yellow, 2 orange, 1 red) and then used the leftover filling for burritos the next day. T'was awesome!
This is the perfect weeknight meal, it is so easy to prepare and tastes fantastic. I did add in diced onion and minced garlic! I will make this again!

I have actually made this several times I usually incorporate adobo peppers, pinto beans, corn, as well as tomatillos to balance out the spice. I also use this to make stuffed cabbage as well. One of the family favorites
I used vegan meat and vegan cheese
Easy to make, tasted great! Spice it up with green chilis as needed.
